chapters.title: The Opportunity

chapters.argument: FIELDWORK is buying attention for a broad design promise before it has proved why a mixed-use household should choose its first object or return for the second.
chapters.decision: Reject this diagnosis if a specific mixed-use proposition does not improve qualified product-page progression and net conversion, or if existing cohorts already show strong second-purchase behaviour.
chapters.title: The Constraint

chapters.argument: FIELDWORK could own the mixed-use surface: modular objects designed for the daily collision of paid work, domestic life and limited space.
chapters.decision: Compare this territory with organisation-led and status-led alternatives on relevance, distinctiveness, willingness to pay and unprompted recall.
chapters.title: The Advantage

chapters.argument: Turn the mixed-use surface into a category FIELDWORK can own, then prove that one useful object earns the next purchase before scaling acquisition.
chapters.decision: Approve only the next tests, not the modelled revenue outcome.

recommendations.action: Organise the proposition around the moments when work and home collide, rather than a broad accessories catalogue.
recommendations.name: Own the mixed-use surface
recommendations.trade_off: A narrower promise may reduce broad but low-intent traffic.

recommendations.action: Merchandise each object through a specific domestic work moment, with dimensions, material decisions and usage proof visible before purchase.
recommendations.name: Make usefulness visible
recommendations.trade_off: More proof requires disciplined production and may expose weak claims.

recommendations.action: Build modular add-on, post-purchase and referral tests that reveal whether the first object creates a repeatable customer system.
recommendations.name: Earn the second object
recommendations.trade_off: Near-term reach grows more slowly while economics are validated.
